question: Which of the following is a strong reducing agent used to reduce aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acid chlorides, carboxylic acids and even carboxylate salts to alcohols?
solution:
The correct answer is Lithium aluminium hydride.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **LiAlH₄** is a **potent**, unselective reducer of polar double bonds that is most often considered to be an** H⁻ source. Aldehydes, ketones, esters, carboxylic acid chlorides, carboxylic acids,** and even **carboxylate** **salts** will all be converted to **alcohols via this process**.
 
• Often referred to as **LAH, lithium aluminium hydride** is an** inorganic substance** with the **chemical formula Li[AlH₄] or LiAlH₄.**
 
• It is a white solid that was found in 1947 by** Finholt, Bond, and Schlesinger**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Titanium hydride**

 
 
• ​In most cases, the term **"titanium hydride" **refers to the **inorganic substance TiH₂** and related **nonstoichiometric substances**. In addition to being utilised as an additive in the creation of **Alnico** sintered magnets, metal foam, powdered titanium metal, and pyrotechnics, it is commercially accessible as a stable grey/black powder.
 
 
 
• **Calcium hydride**
 
 
• **Calcium hydride**, often known as **alkaline earth hydride**, is a **chemical compound** having the formula **CaH2**. This grey powder reacts violently with water to release **hydrogen gas** (white if pure, which is uncommon). **CaH₂** is thus employed as a desiccant or **drying agent**. **CaH2 is a saline hydride**, which means that it has a salt-like structure.
 
 
 
• **Bismuth hydride**
 
 
• ​The **chemical compound** known as **bismuthine** has the formula **BiH₃**. **BiH₃**, the heaviest **analogue of ammonia** (**a pnictogen hydride**), is unstable and breaks down into **bismuth metal at temperatures **well below **zero degrees. **This compound has a **pyramidal structure as predicted, with H-Bi-H angles roughly 90 degrees.**
